body: **Foco:** Non-defining relative clauses — introdução.
**Verbos:** adapt.
**Pronúncia:** Ligações e assimilação.
**20 palavras novas** (ciência).
**Texto do dia:** transcrição de palestra e podcast.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (B2):** eu consigo usar orações relativas explicativas (, which … , whose …) numa palestra de astronomia e usar adapt.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Lecture: A Tour of Our Solar System
paras: Good evening. Jupiter, **which is the largest planet**, has dozens of moons. Saturn, **whose rings are made of ice and rock**, is easy to spot with a small telescope. The Moon, **which orbits Earth in about a month**, controls our tides.
Our guide, **who has studied astronomy for years**, will **adapt** the tour to your questions. Mars, **where scientists search for past life**, is next.

items.q: Jupiter is described as the largest planet.
Saturn’s rings are made of gold.
The guide will adapt the tour.

head: Pronome
Exemplo
rows: Jupiter**, which is the largest planet,** has moons.
Saturn**, whose rings are ice,** is easy to see.
Our guide**, who has studied for years,** will help.
Mars**, where scientists search,** is next.

blocks.body: Cláusulas **não restritivas** acrescentam informação **extra** e vêm **entre vírgulas**. **Não** use **that** nelas e **não** retire o pronome.

items.s: Jupiter, ___ is the largest planet, has moons. (which)
Saturn, ___ rings are ice, is easy to see. (whose)
Our guide, ___ studied for years, will help. (who)
Mars, ___ scientists search for life, is next. (where)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.pt: O que Jupiter tem de especial?

body: **Over the moon.** — Nas nuvens.
**The sky is the limit.** — O céu é o limite.
**Shoot for the moon.** — Mirar na lua.
**Out of this world.** — Fora deste mundo.
**Light years ahead.** — Anos-luz à frente.
**Land on your feet.** — Cair de pé.
**What is special about Jupiter?** — O que Jupiter tem de especial?
**And Saturn?** — E Saturno?
**Jupiter, which is the largest planet, has dozens of moons.** — Júpiter, que é o maior planeta, tem dezenas de luas.

items.label: Ligações e assimilação
items.note: Sons se ligam e se transformam: did you → didja; want you → wanchu; pick it up → pi-ki-dup.

prompts.model: The Moon, which orbits Earth, affects tides.
Saturn, whose rings are famous, is lovely.
My teacher, who loves space, is here.

blocks.task: Write 5 sentences with non-defining relative clauses about space or your town.
blocks.model: Jupiter, which is the largest planet, has many moons. Saturn, whose rings are made of ice, is easy to see. The Moon, which orbits Earth, controls the tides. Our guide, who loves astronomy, is friendly. Mars, where scientists search for life, is next.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
